correctness.rationale: Exact transition alpha*K_t/t implies the conditional gamma-product survival formula. The probability of one prior active step cancels the n-dependent gamma coefficient; a unique first second-step event gives the explicit second coefficient. Since alpha<1, first-class 1/m error is o(m^{-2alpha}); the finite mixture settles moments. Logarithmic product errors are O(n^{-alpha}+n^{alpha-1}) on the local scale. Combining this with Bercu’s established a.s. K_n/n^alpha -> M>0 and the classical E_alpha(-z) asymptotic proves the joint mixture limit and its exponent-one tail. A fresh standalone checker passed 609 exact/numerical finite tests; finite checking alone is not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Compared the precise theorem, not its title, with the original ERWS work, earlier delay-count papers, an equivalent reinforced harmonic success Markov model, and published research records. Count-chain equivalence and known Mittag-Leffler limit are explicitly conceded. The examined primary results do not yield an already-stated deterministic-time forward waiting theorem with a universal fixed-time coefficient, explicit next term and contrasting local scaling tail; prior generalized species-sampling waiting results remain a priority risk. Miyazaki and Takei (arXiv:2003.04441) also derive the exact activity birth chain and its Mittag-Leffler limit, which are credited, not claimed as original; their inspected theorems and appendices concern count variables rather than the new forward waiting law.
residual_risks: Broad species-discovery or Pitman–Yor gap theorems may encode the combined result in different notation; cited Section 8 already contains the count birth process.
The 2025 follow-up arXiv:2503.17586 could only be compared by its abstract and available scope information; no full-document negative originality conclusion rests on it.
Search and available research records are finite and do not prove absolute historical priority.

value.rationale: Forward inactivity is a natural observable of stopped walks, distinct from activity-count growth. The universal finite-time Pareto coefficient and infinite mean hold at every observation time, while the actual local scale has a different limiting Pareto exponent. The explicit positive second coefficient shows how finite-time rare-history terms change with observation time, giving meaningful structural information beyond a known counting theorem.
